title: Orchestrating Reasoning and Reaction: An Asynchronous Hierarchical Framework for LLM-driven Traffic Signal Control

problem.claim: Network-wide coordinated traffic signal control is important for improving urban mobility.

gap.claim: Existing approaches trade off broad observation and coordination against inference cost, spatial-topological hallucinations, and real-time execution constraints.

contributions.claim: Astra is a three-layer asynchronous hierarchical architecture that separates high-level strategic reasoning from reactive traffic-signal execution.
The architecture combines macro-level bottleneck identification and regional partitioning, meso-level topological semantic causal coordination, and micro-level decentralized MARL execution.
Astra uses an asynchronous synergetic protocol with strategic locking and proactive feedback for stable adaptive re-planning.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Evaluations on real-world datasets reportedly show that Astra consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baseline methods.
The authors report superior efficiency, robustness, and generalization across diverse urban scenarios.

narrative_sequence.summary: Network-wide coordinated traffic signal control is framed as important for urban mobility.
Traditional MARL and LLM agents are described as having complementary limitations involving observational scope, inference cost, hallucination, and real-time constraints.
Astra addresses these limitations with a three-layer hierarchy separating strategic reasoning from reactive execution.
An asynchronous protocol provides strategic locking and proactive feedback for stability and adaptive re-planning.
The authors report improved performance and generalization on real-world datasets across urban scenarios.

source_observation.claim: The framework separates low-frequency strategic reasoning from high-frequency reactive execution.

interpretation.claim: Different temporal and spatial responsibilities may be assigned to specialized control layers.

application.claim: Systems combining deliberative models with reactive controllers can consider hierarchical decomposition when latency and coordination scope conflict.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this decomposition transfers beyond traffic signal control or which operating conditions are required.

unknowns: No quantitative results, evaluation metrics, or dataset names are provided.
The abstract does not specify baseline identities, implementation details, or ablation results.
The conditions and scope of the reported generalization are not detailed.
